canonical.name: Local range-oracle contract for verified flow and variational data
canonical.reason: This interface is an explicit local contract needed by the Euler, shooting, and Floquet enclosures.

canonical.name: Bounded inverse for the continuous phase-bordered BVP operator
canonical.reason: The item derives the endpoint shooting matrix and supplies its own operator inverse constant.

canonical.name: Explicit midpoint collocation residual and discretization constants
canonical.reason: The periodic augmented BVP combines the local midpoint theorem with a directly proved residual constant.

canonical.name: Validated shooting residual to trajectory error constant
canonical.reason: The local Taylor and Gronwall argument gives an explicit residual-to-orbit estimate under stated bounds.

canonical.name: Finite pseudo-arclength continuation interface for periodic branches
canonical.reason: The algorithm composes the phase-bordered jet with the declared certified local continuation interface.

canonical.name: Second variation equation and C2 flow regularity on a common tube
canonical.reason: This local intermediate result supplies the C2 regularity needed by the pseudo-arclength branch residual from the C2 field hypothesis.

canonical.name: Finite nonnormal perturbation bound for a separated simple multiplier
canonical.reason: The Schur-complement proof supplies the finite left/right-conditioned correction beyond first order.

sources.title: Y. A. Kuznetsov, Elements of Applied Bifurcation Theory, 2nd ed., Chapter 1, §1.5 and Chapter 3, §§3.4–3.5
sources.locator: Complete 614-page second-edition PDF retrieved; inspected printed pp. 26–30 on transverse sections, return maps, variational equation, monodromy, and phase multiplier.

contents.name: Chapter 1 §1.5: transversal section and local Poincare return map
contents.reason: The local proof derives the quotient conjugacy and exact removal of the phase multiplier rather than importing the book's sketch.

contents.name: Chapter 1 §1.5: variational equation, monodromy and neutral tangent multiplier
contents.reason: The local proof differentiates the autonomous flow identity and checks the nonzero tangent hypothesis.

contents.name: Chapter 3 §§3.4–3.5: Poincare multipliers and orbital stability
contents.reason: The local theorem verifies the least-period reduction, phase multiplier and strict transverse disk conditions before applying orbital stability.

contents.name: Chapter 1 §1.5: transverse section condition at a periodic point
contents.reason: The item proves both directions of the bordered-Jacobian criterion and gives a finite inverse bound.

sources.title: E. J. Doedel and B. E. Oldeman, AUTO-07P: Continuation and Bifurcation Software for ODEs, full manual (2021)
sources.locator: Full 12,856-line manual retrieved; inspected periodic families/Floquet source lines 587–645, ISP warning lines 4926–4950, and phase-shifting demo ph1 lines 6822–6863.

contents.name: Periodic family formulation: periodic endpoint rows and period parameter
contents.reason: The local definition fixes its scaled-time and boundary conventions explicitly and separately states existence and invertibility are not part of the definition.

contents.name: Demo ph1: rescaled time and phase manipulation
contents.reason: The definition states the exact augmented multiple-shooting and normalized midpoint residual rows.

contents.name: ISP section: neutral multiplier and possible inaccuracy of linearized Poincare data
contents.reason: The algorithm encloses the exact variational flow and never treats a raw approximate multiplier as validated.

contents.name: Periodic family endpoint equations and positive period
contents.reason: The local proof establishes the exact correspondence between a residual zero and the scaled periodic solution.

sources.title: S. M. Rump, Verification methods: Rigorous results using floating-point arithmetic, Acta Numerica 19 (2010)
sources.locator: Full 163-page article retrieved; inspected §§10 and 13, including Theorems 13.1–13.3 and the strict-inclusion/Krawczyk proof in §13.3.

contents.name: §13.3, Theorem 13.3: Krawczyk strict inclusion and existence
contents.reason: The local theorem checks the interval residual and Jacobian hypotheses and keeps uniqueness tied to the separate contraction bound.

contents.name: §13: outward interval enclosures and verified nonlinear residuals
contents.reason: The definition specifies exactly which residual, Jacobian, trajectory and monodromy ranges a successful record contains.

contents.name: §§10 and 13: strict interval certificates require outward-valid bounds
contents.reason: Candidate Newton or collocation output is only a candidate until interval inclusion, contraction and nonstationarity checks succeed.

sources.title: R. B. Kearfott, Interval Computations: Introduction, Uses, and Resources, Euromath Bulletin 2(1) (1996)
sources.locator: Full PDF retrieved and verified as 23 pages; inspected §§1–2 on interval sets, outward enclosure, Brouwer, and interval Newton/Krawczyk.

contents.name: §1: represented interval sets and outward inclusion
contents.reason: The finite Euler enclosure uses rational set arithmetic and returns inconclusive whenever the range-oracle or tube test is unavailable.

contents.name: §2: Brouwer-based interval Newton/Krawczyk inclusion
contents.reason: The local proof states the distinct existence and uniqueness conditions needed for an exact periodic root.

contents.name: §2: interval Jacobian mean-value enclosure
contents.reason: The corrector supplies exact residual and Jacobian enclosures to the Krawczyk validator and claims no root from a finite residual alone.

sources.title: J. Lebl, Guide to Cultivating Complex Analysis, Chapter 4 §4.1 and Chapter 5 §5.4
sources.locator: Complete 304-page text retrieved; inspected Chapter 4 §4.1, printed pp. 93–96, and Chapter 5 §5.4, printed pp. 128–132.

contents.name: Chapter 4 §4.1: winding number and local constancy
contents.reason: The local proof establishes the inside-one/outside-zero polygon index using connectivity and the local jump formula.

contents.name: Chapter 5 §5.4, Theorem 5.4.1: argument principle
contents.reason: The local theorem derives the characteristic-polynomial logarithmic derivative and uses its own resolvent and quadrature bounds.

contents.name: Chapter 5 §5.4: logarithmic derivative counts zeros with multiplicity
contents.reason: The algorithm reports a count only when the complex integral enclosure lies in one strict integer neighborhood.

contents.reason: The worked calculation exposes why a raw coarse Euler amplification is not an exact Floquet value.

sources.title: S. M. Rump, Verification methods: Rigorous results using floating-point arithmetic, Acta Numerica 19 (2010), §13
sources.locator: Full 163-page article retrieved; inspected §§10 and 13, including Theorems 13.1–13.3 and the strict-inclusion/Krawczyk proof in §13.3.

contents.name: §13.3: interval root certificates and strict inclusion
contents.reason: The example is explicitly conditional on future validated root and spectral records and claims no computed van der Pol interval.

contents.name: §13: interval enclosures do not decide a claim unless they separate its boundary
contents.reason: The example shows that an enclosure crossing the unit circle cannot prove strict inside or outside placement.
